overall_summary: The channel is experiencing significant traction with extreme cosmic anomalies and space-themed mysteries, particularly those highlighting bizarre planetary conditions (e.g., TrES-2b, burning ice, supersonic rubies). Conversely, repetitive psychological facts (fake memories, songs stuck in head) and basic animal trivia (immortal jellyfish, octopus hearts) are severely underperforming and failing to capture viewer interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' achieved 1,019 views and 36 likes. 'The Planet of Burning Ice' reached 1,055 views. 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' generated 721 views and 25 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space science. Focus on highly visual, hostile exoplanets and cosmic paradoxes using dramatic, high-contrast imagery.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' gained 264 views, showing strong performance compared to standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Produce content explaining counter-intuitive physics, relativity, and time dilation concepts using relatable human scales.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was posted multiple times across different dates and consistently failed to exceed 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic brain hacks and psychological tricks unless they are tied to a shocking, highly original case study.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (immortal jellyfish) generated only 69 views. 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' plateaued at 183 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid entry-level biology facts that are already saturated on YouTube Shorts. Replace with cinematic animal survival narratives.

next_video.concept: The Planet That Is Literally Evaporating Into Space (HD 209458b / Osiris)
next_video.opening_direction: Show a dramatic rendering of a planet with a massive, glowing blue tail, stating: 'This planet is literally melting and leaving a giant tail behind it like a comet.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is so close to its sun that it's being slowly eaten alive, losing 10,000 tons of atmosphere every single second.
next_video.reason: Aligns with the highly successful 21-second duration format of TrES-2b and Supersonic Rubies, leveraging the proven high-performing 'hostile planet' sub-niche.

experiment: Test a cinematic historical storytelling Short about a bizarre ancient mystery (e.g., the Antikythera mechanism or a lost city) to see if the high-retention storytelling style can replicate the success of the space anomaly videos.
